newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended down on Thursday, unable to retain a midsession recovery as profit-takers in a fairly empty market pushed prices down.

On the back of this morning's German December M3 figures, showing a 7.9 percent increase, prices fell in the morning, but dealers said that was digested fairly rapidly, with the market picking up at the midsession.
Dealers said the absence of inspiring news contributed to the bond market's lower prices in the afternoon.
"Some people were possibly disappointed the Dutch Central Bank did not raise its special advances rate (this afternoon at 1500 GMT), and turned to profit-taking," one dealer suggested.
Trade in the new 5.75 February 2007 bond, issued this week, was active, dealers said, adding it was mainly professionals who were on the selling side.
A 10-year bond issued by Dresdner Bank in the afternoon totalling 750 million guilders, added to price pressure, dealers said.
Switching into longer durations continued to hit the short end, causing that part of the curve to flatten, dealers said.
"That has been going on for about two weeks now," one dealer said, adding it started to look like a trend.
